sentences.text: 1 This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 15.12.2021 at about 1.50 p.m. while walking on left side on KFC Junction, near Sangeetha Mobiles, Indiranagar, Bengaluru, a BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F9585 came in high speed on opposite direction rash and negligently and dashed against him, hence he sustained grievous injuries, so that, he was SCCH 5 taken to Chinmaya Mission Hospital, Bengaluru, for which, he had spent an amount of Rs.1,50,000/.
3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 26 years, hale and healthy, working as Operation Executive in Doqfy Company and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m., out of this accident he has lost his income and working capacity, due to this accident crime No.45/2021 is registered against driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

Respondent is ownercumself insurer of the BMTC bus, he is liable to pay compensation, so that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.10,50,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, respondent has appeared and filed written statement denying the case of the petitioner, further denied that accident is occurred due to SCCH 5 negligency of BMTC bus driver,
further petitioner has to prove his age and income and also to prove the medical expenses incurred by him, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly pray to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 15.12.2021 at about 1.50 p.m. near Sangeetha Mobiles, Indiranagar, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F9585 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how mch and from whom?
SCCH 5 3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked 25 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, driver of the BMTC bus has deposed his evidence as RW1, but not marked any documents, accordingly evidence is closed.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH 5 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1:
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of wound certificate is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of spot sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Charge Sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
9.

On perusal of the crossexamination it is noticed that, there is no denial of place, date and time of the accident, at the time of smart city work, this accident is occurred, as per Ex.P.5 hand sketch map accident is occurred within 7 ft. of edge of the road, further admits that, he was not on footpath,
vehicles were not moving on SCCH 5 right side due to running of the white tapping work, hence vehicles were coming on the same way which he had been moving.
Further denied that, he did not observed the bus, further denied that, colluding with the police false case is registered, further denied that, there is no negligency of the bus driver.

10. It is noticed that case is registered against the bus and its driver, charge sheet is also against the bus driver, but Ex.P.5 hand sketch map speaks that, bus came towards left side within 7 ft. of the left edge.

Further it is noticed that, on right side white tapping work was on progress, so that, bus had been moving on the left side of the road, there is a footpath but this petitioner was within 7 ft from the left edge and he was moving on public road, hence bus came on back side and dashed against him.
SCCH 5 11.
On the other hand, driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA01F9585 has deposed his evidence as RW1, wherein stated that very accident is occurred due to negligency of the petitioner.
In crossexamination admits that while moving towards Swami Vivekananda Statute from Silk Board, this accident is occurred.
Further denied that, this accident is occurred on a footpath, he has not lodged complaint, but deposed that he has made arrangement for first aid.

12. On going through the evidence available on record, it is noticed that, very accident is occurred on public road, further it is noticed that, very road is two lane road, left end road was under construction/white tapping, hence bus had been moving on left road, further it is noticed that, there is a footpath on left side of the road, but petitioner had been moving on public road, SCCH 5 after gap of 7 ft of the footpath.
Under such circumstances, it is clear that, petitioner himself has violated the traffic rules and moved on a public road in crowd area.

Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture of left talus with dislocation, for which, he underwent treatment with ORIF with screws and repair of the deltoid ligament.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.3, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9, follow up sheets marked as Ex.P.13, lab reports marked as Ex.P.14, X ray report marked as Ex.P.15, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
15.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS has deposed his evidence as PW2 and furnished OPD slip marked as Ex.P.17, Xray Films na Ex.P.18.
He has assessed physical disability of the left SCCH 5 lower limb at the rate of 54% and whole body disability at the rate of 18%.
16. As per evidence of the Doctor, there is disability to the left lower limb at the rate of 54% after converting to the whole body, disability is at the rate of 18%.

On perusal of the crossexamination he admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner, not gone through the case sheet, not seen any of the documents, fracture is united, but there is loss of range of movements, further denied that, there is no loss of stability component.

17. In support of his case Medical Record Technician of Chinmaya Mission Hospital has deposed his evidence as PW3 and furnished copy of ID card marked as Ex.P.19, authorization letter marked as Ex.P.20, copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.21, copy of Police Intimation marked as Ex.P.22, OPD File marked as SCCH 5 Ex.P.23, IP file marked as Ex.P.24, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.25.
In crossexamination deposed that, he do not know the contents of the documents produced by him.

18. As per case of the petitioner he has taken treatment as indoor patient for 8 days, surgery is conducted, spent an amount of Rs.1,50,000/, on perusal of Ex.P.9 discharge summary it is noticed that, petitioner has taken treatment as indoor patient since 15.12.2021 to 18.12.2021 it reveals that,
he has taken treatment as indoor patient only for 3 days.

Further on perusal of the same it reveals that, surgery is conducted in Chinmaya Mission Hospital on his left leg on 15.12.2021, petitioner was aged about 26 years and working as Operation Executive in Dofqy Company.

Considering the same,
disability to the particular limb is considered at the rate of 30%, after converting disability SCCH 5 is considered to the whole body at the rate of 10%.
Accordingly disability to the whole body is considered at the rate of 10% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

19. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 26 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.8, accordingly he is born on 16.05.1995 and the Sri. For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,39,181/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand One Hundred Eighty One Only) i.e., 80% of Rs.4,23,976/

Remaining 20% compensation of Rs.84,795/ shall be borne by the petitioner.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to SCCH 5 his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,39,181/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand One Hundred Eighty One Only) i.e., 80% of Rs.4,23,976/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization which shall be paid by respondent along with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Remaining 20% compensation of Rs.84,795/ shall be borne by the petitioner.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to SCCH 5 his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
